Voormsi (Vorms) is the national card game of Greenland and is said to be much played on the coastal ferry. It is a trick-taking game descended from the German Brusbart tradition, which in turn derives from Karnöffel, the oldest identifiable European card game with a continuous tradition (first recorded in Nördlingen, Bavaria, 1426). The game is reputed to be ancient; some Greenlanders speculate it may date from the Whaling Period between the disappearance of the Norse settlement and the arrival of Danish missionaries, when European contact was mainly with whalers and pirates. The name vôrmse (voormsi since the 1973 spelling reform) is not of Greenlandic origin; Danish–Greenlandic dictionaries equate Danish brus and vorms to Greenlandic vôrmse. Related games in the same family include Danish Brus, Swedish Bräus, Icelandic Alkort and Treikort, and Polish Drużbart.
